title: Fill in full frame lists and sweep both sheets for near-white at ground contact
tier_reason: Catalog metadata and pixel cleanup on placeholder art, both revertable in git; the taste call on the ground-contact rule stays with Ingrid's look session.
ask: Complete the frame lists in the catalog and sweep every frame of both sheets for opaque near-white in the ground-contact zone, so the fixes land on all frames instead of half.
first_action: Extend the Chicken entry in hq/data/entities.json from 4 to all 8 cells and Farmer from 4 to all 16, then scan each listed cell for opaque near-white pixels in the ground-contact zone.
source_message:
> HQ's sprite editor only showed him a quarter of each sheet. 

Why aren't you also creating a story to fix this?
result:
I filled in the two catalog entries and finished what was half-done.

**Catalog:** Chicken now lists all 8 cells (right walk 0–3, left walk 4–7) instead of just the right-facing 4. Farmer now lists all 16 cells of the 4×4 grid (down/up/left/right × 4-frame walk) instead of just the down row. The HQ sprite editor reads this list, so it can now show and edit every direction of both, not a quarter of the sheet.

**The sweep:** every pixel it found was the exact same color — `#f8f4e6`, opaque — which is the pipeline's flood-fill background key plate. Nothing ambiguous, no white feathers or white shirt buttons caught in it: 75 pixels total, all leftover backdrop trapped in the ground-contact zone across frames Daniel never touched by hand. I erased them the same way he did (alpha to zero, nothing recolored) — 51 in the farmer sheet, 24 in the chicken sheet — so his two hand fixes now cover every frame instead of the 4 of 16 and 4 of 8 he was able to reach through the old preview.

Both sheets sweep clean now. This is pixel cleanup of existing placeholder art, not a new generation, so no new CREDITS.md entry applies.

One thing worth Ravi's attention, already known from the parent thread: this confirms the pipeline's flood-fill keying is the actual source — it can't reach background pockets enclosed by the sprite, so it leaves opaque key-color pixels behind. That's a pipeline fix, already filed to him; I only cleaned up its output here.

Done, not committed — left in the working tree per the house rule. Nothing pushed.
